display.title: Pesach Is Coming: Matzah, the Seder and Inviting a Guest
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains how the Seder lets us relive our freedom, reminds families to get matzah in time, and gives the order of the day: invite someone who has no Seder.
display.summary_long: A short pre-Pesach talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that Pesach, the holiday of our redemption, recalls how Hashem freed the Jewish people from slavery in Egypt with countless miracles, and that we relive that freedom every year at the Seder, where the whole family reads the Haggadah and eats special foods. The Torah commands us to eat matzah on both Seder nights, so now is the time to buy enough matzah, wine and Pesach food for the whole family, with help from a local rabbi if needed. Then comes the order of the day for soldiers in Tzivos Hashem: find a relative or friend who has no Seder of their own and invite them, just as the Haggadah opens with 'Let all who are hungry come and eat.' One mitzvah leads to another, so a Seder invitation can be the start of many more.
display.lesson: Share your Seder: invite someone who has nowhere to go, because one mitzvah leads to another.
